EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A strong winter storm impacted the region from the 3rd to the 5th of January. This produced between 1 to 2 feet of snow in the Tahoe Basin with 2 to 4 feet for the higher elevations. This system also produced winds upwards of 90 mph on the ridges, with gusts commonly upwards of 55 mph elsewhere.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Mount Rose Ski Base reported 25 inches of snow, trained spotter at 1 NNW Incline Village measured 19.5 inches with a SWE of 2.71 inches, and Diamond Peak Ski Base reported 12 inches. These are storm totals.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: After a brief break, the second in a series of strong winter systems impacted western NV and the eastern Sierra from the 18th to 19th. During this time, an additional 1 to 3 feet of snow fell, leading to continued road closures and delays. Also, between 2 to 3 inches of new snow fell in far western NV on the 19th, with lake-enhanced amounts over 8 inches between Reno and Carson City.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: CoCoRaHs station NV-ST-4 measured 6.5 inches of snow. CoCoRaHs station NV-WH-11 measured 4.6 inches of snow. Finally, Reno International Airport measured 4 inches of snow on the 19th.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: The first in a series of strong winter storms impacted the eastern Sierra from the 16th to 17th. In this two day period, upwards of 2 to 4 feet of snow fell, and was accompanied by winds upwards of 80-100 mph. Donner Pass, along with other mountain passes, was closed for over a day. The greatest overall impacts occurred on the 17th when heavy snow of 4-10 inches occurred across the main urban areas of far western NV, and higher amounts between 12-18 inches from bands of heavy Lake Tahoe-enhanced snow between Carson City and Washoe Valley.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Trained spotter 1 NNW Incline Village measured 46 inches of snow from the 15th to 18th. Mt Rose Ski Base measured 52 inches of snow between the 15th to 18th. Finally, Diamond Peak Ski Base measured 59 inches between the 15th to 18th.
